base: Markets: 2,000 histories stitched from US stock, bond and bill returns 1928–2025 (Damodaran, downloaded 2026-10-13) in runs averaging 8 years; international stocks use the US series.
Social Security benefits are cut 17% from 2034 (2026 Trustees Report).
Social Security is computed with the 2026 formula on earnings indexed to the 2024 average wage; future salary counts up to the 2026 taxable maximum.

Survivors keep the larger benefit, from the year the deceased would have reached their claiming age, once the survivor has claimed; the spousal top-up starts once both have claimed and is reduced for the age it starts at; the traditional balance is treated as {person1}'s for required minimum distributions.
Social Security claimed while {person1} is still working, by either spouse, is added to savings and is not taxed.
The mortgage is paid off in 2048; while {person1} still works, the payment is saved from then on.
The mortgage payment stays the same in dollars, so each year it costs less in today's dollars as prices rise.
401(k) deferrals are capped at the 2026 limit of $24,500 (no age-50 catch-up); any excess stays in take-home pay.

Taxes: 2026 federal rules and 2025 California rules (the latest published); brackets stay fixed in today's dollars; half of each taxable-account withdrawal is treated as gain; the tax on a year's withdrawals is estimated from the previous year's; while {person1} works, lever income is taxed on top of their wages.
In retirement, consulting and the spouse's earnings are taxed on one return with withdrawals and Social Security.
Health insurance before Medicare: $24,000 a year until the older spouse is 65, half until the younger is; Medicare Part B $202.90 a month per person from 65.

College: College Board 2025-26 costs for each child's school (tuition and fees, and living costs where chosen), at the share you plan to cover, growing 1% a year above inflation, for two years from 18 (trade or community college) or four; the 529 pays first, and 529 contributions continue while {person1} works and the child is under 18.
Lifespans come from the 2023 Social Security life table; the plan runs until the younger spouse is 95 regardless, and spending does not drop after a death.
Retirement spending is met from cash above a one-year buffer, then taxable, traditional, HSA and Roth, after tax; the house is never sold to fund the plan.
A required minimum distribution beyond the year's need is moved to the taxable bucket after tax. Retirement income beyond the year's spending is saved to the taxable bucket.
